corrections: Separated configurable Prometheus scrape/evaluation intervals from the page's 15-second example, corrected the default to one minute, and described Head, WAL and persistent blocks without calling the Head a two-hour in-memory block.

Corrected the alerting responsibility boundary: Prometheus (or Grafana Alerting for Grafana-managed rules) evaluates expressions, while Alertmanager groups, inhibits, silences and routes notifications.
Corrected the Prometheus sample-count arithmetic, content-negotiation wording and malformed status label matcher.
Qualified OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation coverage, exporter portability and tail-sampling decisions; removed fixed memory guidance and the promise that a decision always sees a complete Trace.
Separated log-to-trace correlation from metric correlation: LogRecords may carry TraceId/SpanId, while aggregate metrics use resource/time correlation or optional exemplars.

Corrected Grafana's persistence model: it normally queries telemetry backends but persists users, dashboards, configuration and alert-related state, and HA requires shared persistence and alerting coordination.
Replaced obsolete or absolute Grafana claims about Prometheus UI capabilities, data-source counts, rule formats and evaluation intervals.

Corrected Burn Rate semantics: 14.4x over one hour represents about 2% of a 30-day budget and would exhaust it in about 50 hours if sustained; documented paired multiwindow conditions and low-traffic caveats.

Recomputed the SLO example's downtime budget and availability, distinguished request/error SLIs from downtime equivalents, and made release freezes an explicit team policy rather than automatic SLO behavior.
Updated Loki storage descriptions to configurable chunks and current TSDB object-store indexing, noted Promtail end of life, and removed endpoint-wide no-loss and implicit deduplication guarantees.
Qualified trace propagation/export as configured behavior and warned that database query text can contain sensitive or high-cardinality data.

Reframed Chaos Mesh pages as illustrative experiment results, qualified Kubernetes recovery and network implementation details, and made metric-based aborts explicit workflow/orchestration behavior rather than an automatic default.

relationSuggestions.reason: Grafana commonly queries Prometheus for dashboards and alert rules, while Prometheus remains an independent metrics and rule-evaluation system.
OpenTelemetry context propagation, SDKs and OTLP provide the mechanism illustrated by the distributed-tracing page.
OpenTelemetry log records and Collector pipelines can feed log backends, while ELK and Loki also support non-OTel ingestion paths.
SLIs and error-budget burn rates can drive Grafana or Prometheus alert rules and dashboard views.
Chaos experiments should define steady-state criteria from user-facing SLIs and respect error-budget and blast-radius policies.
